examples.scenario: Two DTM tiles overlap and the input list order changes between runs.
examples.reason: GDAL mosaic/VRT can use input order as overlap priority; ordering must be serialized before numeric inspection.

examples.scenario: A VRT overlap returns the last source value but source order is undocumented.
examples.reason: Last-source precedence is a result dependency and must be auditable.

examples.scenario: GTI overlap z-order is inferred from filesystem order.
examples.reason: GTI exposes explicit sorting controls; overlap priority must be fixed in metadata.

examples.scenario: A tile has a valid rectangular extent but large internal nodata areas.
examples.reason: Rectangular extent is not equivalent to valid pixel coverage.

examples.scenario: An uncovered area in a VRT reads as zero and zero becomes the parcel minimum.
examples.reason: Uncovered VRT pixels can read as zero when nodata is not explicitly configured.

examples.scenario: Source masks are ignored and the last overlapping source overrides masked pixels.
examples.reason: Mask/nodata compositing policy changes which source contributes at overlap.

examples.scenario: Two tiles have the same CRS but slightly different pixel sizes.
examples.reason: A common CRS does not prove cell-grid congruence.

examples.scenario: Two 1 m tiles have origins offset by half a pixel.
examples.reason: Equal resolution with incongruent origins creates ambiguous seam cells.

examples.scenario: Rotation terms are assumed zero on every tile without readback.
examples.reason: All six geotransform coefficients are part of grid congruence.

examples.scenario: A tile has the same geometry but a different elevation unit.
examples.reason: Mosaicing values with incompatible physical units would corrupt extrema.

examples.scenario: A GTI catalog omits RESX/RESY and adopts resolution from whichever tile opens first.
examples.reason: Catalog resolution must be explicit for deterministic replay.

examples.scenario: Tile index contains an extra stale tile outside the approved source set.
examples.reason: Exact source membership must be digest-bound, not discovered opportunistically.

examples.scenario: A seam has a one-pixel gap and the gap is silently filled with zero.
examples.reason: Missing coverage is a data condition, not a terrain elevation.

examples.scenario: A seam has a one-column overlap and the selected source changes after filename sorting.
examples.reason: Overlap selection cannot depend on incidental filename order.

examples.scenario: Two seam pixels have equal values but come from different source tiles.
examples.reason: Numeric equality does not erase source provenance.

examples.scenario: A VRT query returns the expected value but pixel-info shows a different contributing tile than the golden replay.
examples.reason: Exact result provenance requires the same intended source contribution.

examples.scenario: A VRT uses an overview during a downsampled request and the value matches full resolution.
examples.reason: Derived overview agreement in one case does not authorize overview values as terminal evidence.

examples.scenario: GTI overview extent differs slightly from the full-resolution mosaic.
examples.reason: GDAL documents that mismatched GTI overview extents can yield incorrect subsampled results.

examples.scenario: gdal_merge materialization differs only because the source order changed.
examples.reason: Materialized mosaic bytes depend on overlap precedence.

examples.scenario: A golden mosaic matches pixel values but has a shifted geotransform.
examples.reason: Same values at different spatial addresses are not equivalent terrain evidence.

examples.scenario: A golden mosaic matches metadata but one seam pixel differs.
examples.reason: Metadata equality cannot substitute for exact pixel comparison.

examples.scenario: A tile footprint is computed from an overview instead of native mask pixels.
examples.reason: Coverage QA must not silently downgrade to reduced-resolution validity.

examples.scenario: A clip envelope expands to whole pixel bounds and expanded cells are treated as parcel members.
examples.reason: Extraction bounds are not equivalent to exact parcel membership.

examples.scenario: An out-of-source clip is allowed and zero-filled cells enter extrema.
examples.reason: Outside-source areas must remain fail-closed or nodata.

examples.scenario: Two tiles have equal pixel size and CRS but different nodata values.
examples.reason: Validity semantics must be harmonized explicitly before compositing.

examples.scenario: A source alpha/mask exists but the mosaic recipe ignores it.
examples.reason: Mask/alpha information can change overlap contribution and valid coverage.

examples.scenario: Tile/seam QA completes while canonical point rows remain zero.
examples.reason: Static mosaic guards can advance without fabricating target coordinates or elevations.

examples.scenario: The missing runner ACK is bypassed by launching a second tile-sampling runner.
examples.reason: The continuation contract requires the existing single shared runner.

examples.scenario: Known tile-binding execution blockers are relabeled pending.
examples.reason: Known unresolved execution conditions remain blocked; pending stays zero.

examples.scenario: Batch 72 is presented as a measured parcel height result.
examples.reason: Real height difference still requires canonical points, authoritative boundary, immutable exact tile set, execution, sampling and readback.
